summary: The result group extends a registered three-dimensional, set-defined Dehn invariant to Euclidean 4-space. It covers the definition, the ridge-sum identity for convex 4-polytopes, invariance under scissors congruence, the six regular 4-polytope invariants and the non-congruence corollaries. This is the necessity half of the classical four-dimensional Dehn-Hadwiger-Jessen theory. It is plausibly paper-worthy as a serious note, and it has an identifiable audience among specialists in scissors congruence and valuations, including the K-theoretic line of work, and among formalizers of convex and polytope geometry. The regular-polytope table and the non-congruence statements are routine consequences of classical dihedral angles, and the account says so. The cited sources and numerical facts check out where inspected. The literature account credits the four-dimensional codimension-2 invariant to Jessen and Sah. It cites no work by Hadwiger, who introduced the invariant in general dimension and in whose framework the 4D simplex-versus-cube non-congruence is classical.

findings.message: The literature account leaves out H. Hadwiger. He defined the codimension-2 Dehn invariant (area of codimension-2 faces tensored with the dihedral angle modulo ℚπ) for polytopes in Euclidean n-space and proved its invariance under scissors congruence. It is commonly called the Dehn-Hadwiger invariant, for example in the Encyclopedia of Mathematics entry and in Lagarias-Moews. Hadwiger appears in the submission only as the name of 'higher invariants' that no formalization was found for. The account credits the four-dimensional invariant to Jessen and Sah and presents the 5-cell-versus-tesseract statement as a four-dimensional analogue of Dehn's theorem without saying that this non-congruence is a classical consequence of Hadwiger's invariant. Cite Hadwiger (for example 'Vorlesungen über Inhalt, Oberfläche und Isoperimetrie', Springer, 1957, and his papers on Zerlegungsgleichheit) for the invariant and its necessity, and say that the regular-simplex-versus-cube non-congruence in dimension 4 is classical. That keeps the novelty claim at the set-based definition and the machine check, which is already where the submission's 'What is claimed' section puts it.

internal_notes.message: Checked by hand. cos(arccos(1/4)) gives about 75.52 degrees. π/3 + arccos(−1/4) = π/3 + π − arccos(1/4) = 4π/3 − θ_5 ≈ 164.48 degrees, so θ_600 ≡ −θ_5 mod ℚπ is correct. (1+3√5)/8 ≈ 0.9635 and cos(164.48°) ≈ −0.9635. x = −(1+3√5)/4 satisfies 4x²+2x−11 = 0, which is not monic over ℤ, so x is not an algebraic integer, and 1/2 is not one either. The irrationality argument is sound. The tesseract (90°), 16-cell and 24-cell (120°) and 120-cell (144°) angles are correct and lie in ℚπ.

Jessen 1968 (Math. Scand. 22, 241-256) and Jessen 1972 (Nachr. Akad. Wiss. Göttingen 1972, 47-53, MR 0353150) are confirmed. Lagarias-Moews DCG 13 (1995) 573-583 with doi 10.1007/BF02574064 and its 4D statement are confirmed from a search snippet. Zakharevich arXiv:1101.3833 is confirmed as 'Scissors Congruence as K-theory'; its dimension 3 and 4 complete / dimension ≥5 open remark could not be checked from the abstract, but it is standard and matches the literature. Dupont 2001 and Sah 1979 are disclosed as unread or partly read; the disclosure is honest. The phrase 'Dupont and Sah later gave proofs through group homology' should ideally cite Dupont-Sah, 'Scissors congruences II', J. Pure Appl. Algebra 25 (1982). This is a minor bibliographic point.

Novelty is not required. The four-dimensional invariance theorem is a classical, paper-level result (Hadwiger, Jessen). Defining the invariant from the point set through cones of directions and Hausdorff measure, rather than from a face list, adds real content and matches the precedent of the registered 3D entry. The risk is a reading of the result as a light repackaging of that entry one dimension up. Against this, the ridge-sum identity and the hyperplane-cut bridge in 4D need genuinely new geometric-measure arguments (2-dimensional strata, lineality planes), which keeps it above the floor. Items 4 and 5 alone would not clear the floor; they are corollaries. The audience is specialists in scissors congruence, Hilbert's third problem, valuations and K-theory, and formalizers of polytope geometry.

No 4D Dehn invariant formalization was found in any system named. This is consistent with my expectations, but I did not search for it independently. No priority is claimed from the table; the submission states that it follows at once from the classical angles.

what_would_reach_higher: Cite Hadwiger for the codimension-2 (Dehn-Hadwiger) invariant in Eⁿ and its invariance under scissors congruence (Vorlesungen über Inhalt, Oberfläche und Isoperimetrie, 1957, and his Zerlegungsgleichheit papers), and credit the four-dimensional invariant as Dehn-Hadwiger, used by Jessen, not as Jessen's and Sah's alone.

State that the regular-simplex-versus-cube non-congruence in dimension 4 (and in every dimension ≥ 3) is classical through Hadwiger-type invariants, so item 5 is presented as a machine check of known facts.

Cite Dupont-Sah, 'Scissors congruences II', J. Pure Appl. Algebra 25 (1982), for the group-homology proofs, and read at least the relevant chapter of Dupont 2001 (freely available from the author) instead of marking it unread.
Confirm the Zakharevich remark on dimensions ≥ 5 with an exact location (paper and section), or replace it with a source that states it directly.

Strengthen the research-interest case by naming what the set-based definition enables that face-list definitions do not, for example applying the bridge to finite unions or non-convex polytopes without a chosen triangulation, or a route towards Jessen's sufficiency theorem. Make item 3 (the bridge) the headline theorem, with items 4 and 5 as corollaries.

If the scope can grow, prove the four-dimensional sufficiency direction for a specific pair (for example an explicit dissection of the 24-cell or the 16-cell into a cube of equal volume, or the zero-invariant case via Jessen). That would lift the group well above a dimension-raised repackaging of the 3D entry.
